newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-BALTIC BOURSE NEEDS RIGHT RULES.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-BALTIC BOURSE NEEDS RIGHT RULES.

text.p: The three Baltic states need to get the right regulations in place before their national stock exchanges can form a pan-Baltic stock market, Riga stock exchange president Uldis Cerps said on Wednesday.
But he said that once the market have developed the chances for cooperation are good.
"What we need to do is really to make sure that there are the necessary regulations in place. A lot of things need to be done in all three Baltic states," Cerps told Reuters in an interview.
Cerps added that all markets need strong watchdogs to be successful. Both intermediaries and listed companies need to be supervised.
"You need to have a strong regulator of the local market who can not only write good laws but also monitor compliance and punish," he said.
Without a stable environment, investors will demand higher rates of return from investment, said Cerps.
"It is very clear that noone wants to invest in an unregulated market."
He added that the chances for a Baltic stock market cooperation are good once the three markets have developed into more mature markets.
"There are good prospects for Baltic cooperation, but there have to be strong partners," Cerps said.
From the middle of this year, Estonia and Latvia will start a cooperation that will allow Latvian investors to keep Estonian shares in Latvian accounts and vice versa.
